words.enDefinition: The use of graphical forms to communicate information in data.

examples.en: We used data visualisation to show how library visits changed over the teaching term.
examples.zh: 我们用「数据可视化」展示图书馆到访量在教学学期内的变化。

examples.en: The data visualisation for our class report shows when the garden received the most rain.
examples.zh: 课堂报告里的「数据可视化」展示了花园在哪个时段降雨最多。

words.enDefinition: The mapping of values or categories to graphical features such as position, size, or colour.

examples.en: The tutor changed the visual encoding so that shape showed the category instead of colour.
examples.zh: 老师更改了「视觉编码」，改用形状表示类别。

examples.en: We checked that the visual encoding used longer bars for larger values throughout the figure.
examples.zh: 我们确认整张图的「视觉编码」都用较长的条形表示较大的数值。

words.enDefinition: A visible element such as a point, line, or rectangle that represents data in a chart.

examples.en: Each graphical mark in the diagram represents one reading from the greenhouse temperature log.
examples.zh: 图中的每个「图形标记」表示温室温度日志中的一次读数。

examples.en: The class selected a rectangle as the graphical mark for each category in its chart.
examples.zh: 全班选择用矩形作为图中每个类别的「图形标记」。

words.enDefinition: A single plotted observation or value in a chart.

examples.en: Each data point shows the measured height of one sunflower in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 课堂示例中的每个「数据点」表示一株向日葵的实测高度。

examples.en: The highlighted data point marks the busiest day in the sample library attendance records.
examples.zh: 突出显示的「数据点」代表示例图书馆客流记录里最繁忙的一天。

words.enDefinition: A set of related values treated as a group in a chart.

examples.en: The chart includes one data series for each of the three gardens in our exercise.
examples.zh: 练习图中的三个花园各有一个「数据系列」。

examples.en: We made the second data series a dashed line to distinguish it from the first.
examples.zh: 我们把第二个「数据系列」画成虚线，使它与第一个区分开。

words.enDefinition: The axis that runs from left to right on a standard two-dimensional plot.

examples.en: The horizontal axis shows the months of the year in the class rainfall chart.
examples.zh: 课堂降雨量图的「横轴」显示一年中的各个月份。

examples.en: We checked where the horizontal axis crosses the vertical axis on the worksheet figure.
examples.zh: 我们在练习图上查看了「横轴」与纵轴的交点。

words.enDefinition: The axis that runs up and down on a standard two-dimensional plot.

examples.en: The vertical axis gives the total number of books loaned each month in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中的「纵轴」显示每月借出的图书总量。

examples.en: We extended the vertical axis so that the highest point was visible on the chart.
examples.zh: 我们延长了「纵轴」的显示范围，让图上可以看到最高点。

words.enDefinition: Text identifying the variable or unit represented along an axis.

examples.en: The axis label states that rainfall is measured in millimetres on the garden chart.
examples.zh: 花园图上的「轴标签」说明降雨量以毫米为单位。

examples.en: I changed the axis label after noticing that the plot shows hours rather than minutes.
examples.zh: 我发现图里按小时计量，于是修改了「轴标签」。

words.enDefinition: A small line on an axis marking a position on its scale.

examples.en: Each tick mark on the plot shows a ten-minute step on the time scale.
examples.zh: 图上每条「刻度线」表示时间标度上的十分钟间隔。

examples.en: We added a tick mark at zero to make the baseline easier to locate.
examples.zh: 我们在零处加了一条「刻度线」，让基线更容易找到。

words.enDefinition: The printed number or category name next to a marked position on an axis.

examples.en: The last tick label shows December at the far right of the rainfall graph.
examples.zh: 降雨量图最右侧的「刻度标签」显示十二月。

examples.en: The tutor shortened a tick label because it overlapped the next month on the axis.
examples.zh: 一个「刻度标签」与轴上下一个月份的文字重叠了，老师便缩短了它。

words.enDefinition: A guide line across the chart area that corresponds to a position on an axis.

examples.en: The light grey gridline helps readers see that the weekly count reaches exactly twenty.
examples.zh: 浅灰色的「网格线」让读者看出周计数恰好达到二十。

examples.en: We removed one gridline that crossed the note and made the text hard to read.
examples.zh: 我们删去了一条穿过注释并让文字难以辨认的「网格线」。

words.enDefinition: An explanatory key linking a chart's graphical features to the series or categories they represent.

examples.en: The chart legend explains which line represents each of the towns in our rainfall comparison.
examples.zh: 「图例」说明降雨量对比图中的每条线分别代表哪个城镇。

examples.en: We moved the chart legend beside the plot so it would not cover the data.
examples.zh: 我们把「图例」移到绘图区旁边，以免遮挡数据。

words.enDefinition: The region of a chart where the data marks are drawn.

examples.en: The note sits above the plot area and leaves the data points easy to see.
examples.zh: 注释放在「绘图区」上方，数据点依然清楚可见。

examples.en: We widened the plot area to make more room for the weekly data on the right.
examples.zh: 我们加宽了「绘图区」，给右侧的周数据留出更多空间。

words.enDefinition: The interval of values from the lower limit to the upper limit of an axis.

examples.en: The axis range runs from zero to fifty in both charts of weekly library visits.
examples.zh: 两张图书馆每周客流图的「轴范围」都是零到五十。

examples.en: We kept the axis range the same so that both panels could be compared directly.
examples.zh: 我们让「轴范围」保持一致，以便直接比较两幅子图。

words.enDefinition: A scale on which equal numerical differences take up equal distances.

examples.en: The linear scale on our rainfall graph puts each additional millimetre the same distance apart.
examples.zh: 降雨量图的「线性标度」上，每增加一毫米，所占间距都相同。

examples.en: We kept a linear scale because the class wanted to compare absolute differences in temperature.
examples.zh: 因为全班想比较温度的绝对差值，我们保留了「线性标度」。

words.enDefinition: A scale on which equal ratios take up equal distances.

examples.en: The logarithmic scale places each tenfold increase the same distance apart in our example.
examples.zh: 示例的「对数标度」上，每一次十倍增长所占的间距相同。

examples.en: Our class used a logarithmic scale to display values spanning several powers of ten.
examples.zh: 我们班用「对数标度」显示跨越多个数量级的数值。

words.enDefinition: A reference line at zero from which a chart measures values such as bar lengths.

examples.en: The chart uses a zero baseline so the library counts can be compared by bar length.
examples.zh: 图表采用「零基线」，读者可以通过条形长度比较图书馆的计数。

examples.en: The tutor checked that every bar in our spending example starts at the zero baseline.
examples.zh: 老师确认支出示例里的每个条形都从「零基线」开始。

words.enDefinition: An axis displayed over a narrower range that omits part of the underlying scale.

examples.en: The truncated axis makes the modest change in library visits look much larger than it is.
examples.zh: 「截断轴」让图书馆到访量的小幅变化看起来大得多。

examples.en: The worksheet asks whether the truncated axis makes the difference between the two bars misleading.
examples.zh: 练习题问「截断轴」是否会让两根条形的差异产生误导。

words.enDefinition: A chart that uses bar lengths to show the values of different categories.

examples.en: The bar chart compares the number of books borrowed from each section of the classroom library.
examples.zh: 「条形图」比较了班级图书角不同区域的图书借阅量。

examples.en: We chose a horizontal bar chart because the names would not fit below vertical bars.
examples.zh: 类别名称太长，排不进竖向条形的下方，所以我们改用了横向「条形图」。

words.enDefinition: A bar chart that places bars for related groups side by side within each category.

examples.en: The grouped bar chart puts last year and this year side by side for each month.
examples.zh: 「分组条形图」把每个月去年的数值与今年的数值并排显示。

examples.en: We used a grouped bar chart to compare morning and evening attendance across three workshops.
examples.zh: 我们用「分组条形图」比较三个工作坊上午和晚上的出席人数。

words.enDefinition: A bar chart in which the segments within each bar show parts of its total.

examples.en: The stacked bar chart shows how fiction and nonfiction loans contribute to each month's total.
examples.zh: 「堆叠条形图」显示小说和非小说借阅量分别占月度总量的多少。

examples.en: Our stacked bar chart uses a separate pattern for each section of the sample library.
examples.zh: 我们的「堆叠条形图」用不同的图案表示示例图书馆的各个区域。

words.enDefinition: A chart that connects values along an ordered variable, often time, with line segments.

examples.en: The line chart follows the temperature in the teaching greenhouse over seven consecutive days.
examples.zh: 「折线图」呈现了教学温室连续七天的温度变化。

examples.en: We used a line chart because the order of the weekly readings matters in this exercise.
examples.zh: 练习里每周读数的先后顺序很重要，所以我们用了「折线图」。

words.enDefinition: A chart that fills the space between a line and a reference level to emphasize magnitude.

examples.en: The area chart fills the space below the line showing weekly rainfall in the sample garden.
examples.zh: 「面积图」填充了示例花园每周降雨量曲线下方的区域。

examples.en: We compared an area chart with a line chart built from the same classroom temperature records.
examples.zh: 我们比较了同一组课堂温度记录生成的「面积图」和折线图。

words.enDefinition: A chart that positions points using paired numerical values to show a relationship or pattern.

examples.en: The scatter plot shows the relationship between hours of sunlight and plant height in our exercise.
examples.zh: 「散点图」展示了练习中光照时长和植物高度之间的关系。

examples.en: In the scatter plot, each greenhouse plant contributes one point with a height and a leaf count.
examples.zh: 在「散点图」中，每株温室植物对应一个点，具有高度和叶片数两个数值。

words.enDefinition: a chart grouping numeric observations into intervals, with each bar's area representing the frequency or proportion in its interval

examples.en: We used a histogram to show how the measured plant heights were distributed across intervals.
examples.zh: 我们用「直方图」展示实测植物高度在各区间内的分布。

examples.en: The histogram has its tallest bar in the middle interval of the example rainfall measurements.
examples.zh: 示例降雨量数据的「直方图」中，最高的条形位于中间区间。

words.enDefinition: A chart that summarizes a numerical distribution with a quartile box, median, and whiskers.

examples.en: The box plot shows that the middle half of the sunflower measurements covers a narrow range.
examples.zh: 「箱线图」显示向日葵测量值中间一半的跨度较窄。

examples.en: We used a box plot for each greenhouse to compare the spread of the plant heights.
examples.zh: 我们为每座温室各画一个「箱线图」，比较植株高度的离散程度。

words.enDefinition: A line extending from a box on a box plot to a defined limit beyond the quartile.

examples.en: The upper whisker ends at the highest value within the rule used on our worksheet.
examples.zh: 在练习规定的范围内，「箱线图的上须」止于最高值。

examples.en: The caption explains what each whisker represents for the plant height measurements in the exercise.
examples.zh: 图注解释了练习的植株高度测量图中，每条「箱线图的须」代表什么。

words.enDefinition: A chart that shows a numerical distribution as a mirrored density shape.

examples.en: The violin plot is widest where the estimated density of plant heights is highest in our example.
examples.zh: 示例「小提琴图」在植物高度估计密度最高的位置最宽。

examples.en: We used a violin plot for each group so readers could compare the shapes of their distributions.
examples.zh: 我们给每组各画一个「小提琴图」，让读者能够比较分布形状。

words.enDefinition: A chart that uses colour shades or intensities to represent values across positions in a grid or space.

examples.en: The heat map shows library attendance by hour and day using a shade for each value.
examples.zh: 「热图」按小时和日期展示图书馆客流量，用色阶表示各个数值。

examples.en: We added a key to the heat map so readers could interpret the darkest cells.
examples.zh: 我们给「热图」添加图例，方便读者理解颜色最深的单元格。

words.enDefinition: a map showing rates, proportions or other statistical values by colouring geographic areas according to their assigned values

examples.en: The choropleth map shades each district according to its share of households with a public library nearby.
examples.zh: 「分级设色地图」按比例为各区着色，该比例表示住在公共图书馆附近的住户所占份额。

examples.en: The tutor asked why the choropleth map uses a rate instead of the raw district count.
examples.zh: 老师问「分级设色地图」为何用比率来着色，而非各区的原始计数。

words.enDefinition: A set of comparable charts using the same design for different subsets or categories.

examples.en: Small multiples let us compare four gardens without drawing every rainfall line on the same axes.
examples.zh: 借助「小多图」，我们可以比较四个花园，无需把所有降雨量线条画在同一组坐标轴上。

examples.en: The report uses small multiples to give each month its own panel with the same scale.
examples.zh: 报告用「小多图」给每个月单独安排一幅子图，并保持标度一致。

words.enDefinition: One panel in a chart that displays a particular subset of the data.

examples.en: Each facet shows a different garden while the scales stay fixed across the rows.
examples.zh: 每幅「分面子图」显示一个不同的花园，各行采用相同标度。

examples.en: We switched the order of two months so the first facet would show April.
examples.zh: 我们调换了两个月份的顺序，使第一幅「分面子图」显示四月。

words.enDefinition: A line attached to a plotted value showing a specified range of uncertainty or variation.

examples.en: The caption explains what each error bar measures around the average plant height in the example.
examples.zh: 图注解释了示例中平均株高旁每条「误差线」表示什么。

examples.en: We added an error bar to each average and explained the chosen range below the plot.
examples.zh: 我们给每个平均值加上一条「误差线」，并在图下说明所选范围。

words.enDefinition: A line drawn on a chart to summarize the overall direction or pattern in the data.

examples.en: The trend line rises across the example scatter plot of sunshine hours and plant height.
examples.zh: 在光照时数与植物高度的示例散点图中，「趋势线」向上倾斜。

examples.en: We added a trend line to highlight the gradual increase in weekly visits to the library.
examples.zh: 我们加了一条「趋势线」，突出图书馆每周客流量逐渐上升的变化。

words.enDefinition: A chart that connects values at two positions to show how several items changed between them.

examples.en: The slope chart connects spring and autumn totals for each of the three reading groups.
examples.zh: 「斜率图」用线段连接三个阅读小组各自的春季和秋季总量。

examples.en: Our slope chart makes it easy to see which garden moved ahead of the others.
examples.zh: 我们的「斜率图」让人容易看出哪个花园后来超过了其他花园。

words.enDefinition: A chart that represents quantities or the distribution of observations with dots along a scale.

examples.en: The dot plot makes it easy to count how many plants have each recorded height.
examples.zh: 「点图」让人容易数出每个记录高度分别对应多少株植物。

examples.en: We used a dot plot to show each group's total on one shared numerical axis.
examples.zh: 我们用「点图」把各组总量显示在同一条数值轴上。

words.enDefinition: A circular chart whose slices represent the shares that categories contribute to a whole.

examples.en: The pie chart shows how the sample library's total loans are divided among book categories.
examples.zh: 「饼图」展示示例图书馆的借阅总量在各类图书之间的分布。

examples.en: We labelled each slice of the pie chart with its percentage of the total.
examples.zh: 我们在「饼图」的每一块扇区上标出它占总量的百分比。

words.enDefinition: A chart in which the position and size of each circular mark encode different values.

examples.en: The bubble chart uses circle area to show each garden's total number of plants.
examples.zh: 「气泡图」用圆的面积表示各花园的植物总数。

examples.en: The worksheet asks which variables determine each circle's position in the bubble chart.
examples.zh: 练习题问的是哪些变量决定「气泡图」中每个圆的位置。

words.enDefinition: A chart that uses nested rectangles sized by value to show parts within a hierarchy.

examples.en: The treemap shows the space occupied by different categories of books on the sample shelves.
examples.zh: 「矩形树图」显示示例书架上不同类别的书占用多大空间。

examples.en: We used a treemap to compare how study materials are distributed across folders and their subfolders.
examples.zh: 我们用「矩形树图」比较学习资料在各文件夹及其子文件夹中的分布情况。

words.enDefinition: A chart that connects two dots on a shared scale to show a difference for each category.

examples.en: The dumbbell plot connects the morning and afternoon visitor counts for each example library branch.
examples.zh: 「哑铃图」把每家示例图书馆分馆上午和下午的访客数连接起来。

examples.en: We read the gap between the two dots for October on the dumbbell plot.
examples.zh: 我们在「哑铃图」上读取十月对应的两个点相距多远。

words.enDefinition: A stacked bar chart in which every bar totals 100 percent and its segments show proportional shares.

examples.en: The 100 percent stacked bar chart compares shares of fiction and nonfiction loans across branches.
examples.zh: 「百分比堆叠条形图」比较各分馆小说和非小说借阅所占比例。

examples.en: Every bar has the same total length in our 100 percent stacked bar chart.
examples.zh: 我们的「百分比堆叠条形图」中，每条的总长度都相同。

collocations: build a 100 percent stacked bar chart
read a 100 percent stacked bar chart
segments of a 100 percent stacked bar chart

words.enDefinition: The obscuring of data patterns when many marks overlap in the same region of a chart.

examples.en: Overplotting makes the dense cluster of repeated plant heights look like just a few points.
examples.zh: 由于「数据点重叠」，大量重复的株高看起来只有几个点。

examples.en: The class found overplotting where several days had the same rainfall and temperature readings.
examples.zh: 全班发现有几天的降雨量与温度读数相同，出现了「数据点重叠」。

words.enDefinition: Points displayed at slightly offset positions so coincident or crowded observations can be seen separately.

examples.en: The jittered points spread sideways just enough to reveal repeated heights in the same group.
examples.zh: 「抖动点」在水平方向上略微分散，显出同一组里重复的株高。

examples.en: We used jittered points so that identical library counts no longer hid behind one another.
examples.zh: 我们用了「抖动点」，让相同的图书馆客流计数能各自显现。

collocations: show jittered points over a box plot

words.enDefinition: The degree to which a plotted point blocks what is behind it.

examples.en: Lower point opacity lets overlapping marks darken where the classroom observations are most concentrated.
examples.zh: 降低「点的不透明度」后，课堂观测值较集中的位置会由于标记重叠而显得更深。

examples.en: We adjusted point opacity so the pale gridlines stayed visible through the printed marks.
examples.zh: 我们调整了「点的不透明度」，使印出的标记下仍能看见浅色网格线。

words.enDefinition: A colour scale for ordered values that typically changes smoothly from lighter to darker shades.

examples.en: The sequential colour scale uses darker shades for greater rainfall in the garden chart.
examples.zh: 花园图的「顺序色标」用较深的颜色表示较大的降雨量。

examples.en: We added a key to explain how the sequential colour scale represents increasing library attendance.
examples.zh: 我们加了一个图例，说明「顺序色标」如何表示图书馆客流量的递增。

words.enDefinition: A colour scale with contrasting colours on the two sides of a meaningful midpoint.

examples.en: The diverging colour scale uses different hues above and below zero in our temperature chart.
examples.zh: 示例温度图的「发散色标」在零点上下采用不同色相。

examples.en: We used a diverging colour scale to distinguish readings above and below the long-term average.
examples.zh: 我们用「发散色标」区分高于与低于长期平均值的读数。

words.enDefinition: A colour scale that uses distinct colours to differentiate categories without implying rank or order.

examples.en: The categorical colour scale assigns a different hue to each of the three reading groups.
examples.zh: 「分类色标」给三个阅读小组各分配一种不同的色相。

examples.en: We used a categorical colour scale because the garden names have no natural numerical order.
examples.zh: 我们用「分类色标」，因为花园名称本身没有数值顺序。

words.enDefinition: The practice of placing explanatory text next to the chart marks it describes.

examples.en: Direct labelling places each garden's name at the end of its rainfall line on the chart.
examples.zh: 「直接标注」把每个花园的名称放在其降雨量线条的末端。

examples.en: We used direct labelling to identify the groups on the printed black and white chart.
examples.zh: 我们用「直接标注」标识黑白印刷图中的各个组别。

words.enDefinition: Text next to a plotted mark that gives its value or another identifying detail.

examples.en: The data label above each bar gives the number of visitors recorded for that week.
examples.zh: 每根条形上方的「数据标签」显示该周记录的访客量。

examples.en: We removed one data label because it covered the point from the following day.
examples.zh: 有一个「数据标签」挡住了次日的数据点，我们把它删掉了。

words.enDefinition: A note or graphical callout that adds context to a specific feature of a chart.

examples.en: The chart annotation explains why the building was closed during the third week of the term.
examples.zh: 「图表注释」说明了该楼在学期第三周关闭的原因。

examples.en: We shifted the chart annotation so its arrow still pointed to the correct reading.
examples.zh: 我们移动了「图表注释」，同时让箭头继续指向正确的读数。

words.enDefinition: A line drawn at a particular value to guide comparisons in a chart.

examples.en: The reference line marks the average monthly visitor count on the class example chart.
examples.zh: 课堂示例图中的「参考线」标出月均访客数量。

examples.en: We drew a reference line at the garden's usual rainfall level for this month.
examples.zh: 我们在花园本月的通常降雨量处画了一条「参考线」。

words.enDefinition: Text accompanying a chart to identify the figure and explain its meaning or context.

examples.en: The chart caption explains that the two panels cover different months of the same year.
examples.zh: 「图注」说明两幅子图呈现同一年里的不同月份。

examples.en: We added the measurement unit to the chart caption for readers using the printed handout.
examples.zh: 我们把计量单位写进「图注」，方便看纸质讲义的读者。

words.enDefinition: A note that identifies the source of the data in a chart, table, or report.

examples.en: The source note names the municipal dataset used for the example map in our report.
examples.zh: 「来源说明」列出报告示例地图使用的市政数据集名称。

examples.en: We added the edition date to the source note beneath the example library chart.
examples.zh: 我们在示例图书馆图表下方的「来源说明」里加了版本日期。

collocations: cite data in a source note

words.enDefinition: A chart title that states the main finding the author wants readers to notice.

examples.en: The takeaway title tells readers that library visits nearly doubled during the final week.
examples.zh: 「结论式图表标题」告诉读者，最后一周的图书馆到访量几乎翻倍。

examples.en: We wrote a takeaway title after checking whether the chart supported our main point.
examples.zh: 确认图表能支持主要观点后，我们写了一个「结论式图表标题」。

words.enDefinition: An extended text alternative that conveys details of a complex image or chart.

examples.en: The long description explains the trend and gives the exact values shown in the figure.
examples.zh: 「详细替代说明」解释了趋势，还给出图中显示的精确数值。

examples.en: The link next to the rainfall chart opens a long description of the key trends.
examples.zh: 降雨量图旁的链接会打开一份说明主要趋势的「详细替代说明」。

collocations: long description for a complex image

words.enDefinition: A data table structured so readers can navigate and interpret the values using assistive technology.

examples.en: The accessible data table lists the rainfall values that are also shown in the chart.
examples.zh: 「无障碍数据表」列出图中也显示的降雨量数值。

examples.en: We tested whether the column headers in the accessible data table made sense when read aloud.
examples.zh: 我们试听了「无障碍数据表」中的列标题，确认读出时是否容易理解。

words.enDefinition: The appearance of a plotted line, such as solid, dashed, or dotted.

examples.en: We gave each rainfall series a different line style for the black and white handout.
examples.zh: 我们为每个降雨量系列设置不同的「线型」，方便在黑白讲义里辨认。

examples.en: The tutor changed the line style of the reference line to distinguish it from the data.
examples.zh: 老师更改了参考线的「线型」，以便将参考线和数据区分开。

words.enDefinition: A visible feature such as a shape, pattern, or label that conveys information without relying on colour.

examples.en: Distinct dash patterns provide a colour-independent cue for the three reading groups on our chart.
examples.zh: 在图表中，三种不同的虚线图案为三个阅读小组提供了「不依赖颜色的提示」。

examples.en: The class used a colour-independent cue by placing each group's name next to its line.
examples.zh: 全班把各组名称放在线条旁边，作为「不依赖颜色的提示」。

words.enDefinition: the contrast of an essential graphic or visible interface component against its adjacent colours

examples.en: We checked non-text contrast to ensure the pale bars remained visible against the chart background.
examples.zh: 我们检查「非文本对比度」，确认浅色条形在图表背景上仍看得清。

examples.en: The tutor demonstrated non-text contrast by comparing two outlines around identical bars on the screen.
examples.zh: 老师对比屏幕上相同条形的两种轮廓，演示「非文本对比度」。

words.enDefinition: A numerical comparison of the relative luminance of two colours.

examples.en: The contrast ratio increased when we darkened the axis labels against the pale chart background.
examples.zh: 我们把浅色背景上的轴标签调深后，「对比度比值」变大了。

examples.en: We recorded the contrast ratio for each pair of colours used in the sample graphic.
examples.zh: 我们记录了示例图中每一对颜色的「对比度比值」。

words.enDefinition: Decorative or distracting features that add no useful meaning to a data chart.

examples.en: We removed the fake shadows as chart junk so the bar lengths were easier to compare.
examples.zh: 我们把模拟阴影当作「图表装饰冗余」删掉，让条形长度更容易比较。

examples.en: The group agreed that the heavy decorative borders were chart junk in the tiny printed figure.
examples.zh: 大家一致认为，粗装饰边框在这张小幅印刷图中属于「图表装饰冗余」。

words.enDefinition: A chart that responds to reader actions to reveal or change the information shown.

examples.en: The interactive chart lets readers select a month and see the corresponding library visitor counts.
examples.zh: 「交互式图表」让读者选一个月份，查看相应的图书馆访客量。

examples.en: We checked that the interactive chart could be used without a mouse during the demonstration.
examples.zh: 演示中，我们确认了不用鼠标也能操作「交互式图表」。

words.enDefinition: A small information box that appears when a reader interacts with a chart feature.

examples.en: The chart tooltip gives the exact rainfall value when a reader selects a plotted bar.
examples.zh: 读者选择某根条形时，「图表浮动提示」会给出精确的降雨量。

examples.en: Our chart tooltip displays the full name of the garden and the date of the reading.
examples.zh: 我们的「图表浮动提示」显示花园的全名以及读数日期。

words.enDefinition: An axis or scale used by more than one plot to make the displays comparable.

examples.en: The two plots use a shared axis for time so the same weeks line up.
examples.zh: 两幅图的时间维度采用「共用坐标轴」，因此相同周次的位置对齐。

examples.en: We retained a shared axis when dividing the rainfall chart into separate panels for each garden.
examples.zh: 我们把降雨量图按花园分为不同子图时，保留了「共用坐标轴」。

words.enDefinition: The ability to obtain consistent computational results using the same inputs and the same analysis procedures.

examples.en: The teaching assistant assessed computational reproducibility by regenerating the plots from the submitted data and code.
examples.zh: 助教用提交的数据和代码重新生成图表，以评估「计算可复现性」。

examples.en: Our report discusses computational reproducibility and lists the tools used to generate every figure.
examples.zh: 我们的报告讨论了「计算可复现性」，还列出生成各图所用的工具。

words.enDefinition: A scripted chain of analysis steps that can regenerate outputs from recorded inputs and settings.

examples.en: A reproducible analytical pipeline generated the garden statistics and the corresponding chart for our report.
examples.zh: 「可复现分析流程」为我们的报告生成了花园统计数据和对应图表。

examples.en: We drew the reproducible analytical pipeline as three stages with the input and output labelled.
examples.zh: 我们把「可复现分析流程」画成三个阶段，并标明输入和输出。

words.enDefinition: A relationship in which a workflow task requires an input or result from another task.

examples.en: The workflow dependency means the chart waits until the regional totals are ready to use.
examples.zh: 这项「工作流依赖关系」意味着只有各区总量准备好，才能生成图表。

examples.en: We drew an arrow for each workflow dependency between the script and the final table.
examples.zh: 我们在脚本和最终表格之间，用箭头标出了每项「工作流依赖关系」。

words.enDefinition: information documenting the origin and processing history of a data item or dataset

examples.en: The data provenance records which rainfall file the team used and who corrected its labels.
examples.zh: 「数据溯源信息」记载了团队使用的降雨量文件，以及谁更正了标签。

examples.en: We checked data provenance before combining two public spreadsheets with similar names and different dates.
examples.zh: 两份公开电子表格的名称相近但日期不同，我们合并它们前核查了「数据溯源信息」。

words.enDefinition: a chain tracing data from their sources through processing steps and on to the datasets or outputs that depend on them

examples.en: The data lineage links the monthly percentages to the original counts and the calculation step.
examples.zh: 「数据血缘」将月度百分比追溯至原始计数和计算步骤。

examples.en: We drew the data lineage to show how two source tables feed the same figure.
examples.zh: 我们画出「数据血缘」，说明同一张图的输入数据来自哪两张源表。

words.enDefinition: An individual entry that documents the origin, handling, or processing history of a data item.

examples.en: The provenance record lists the source file, download date, and translation of the column labels.
examples.zh: 「溯源记录」列出了源文件、下载日期和列标签的翻译。

examples.en: We created a provenance record for the survey table supplied by our fictional community group.
examples.zh: 我们为虚构社区小组提供的问卷表建立了一份「溯源记录」。

words.enDefinition: A reference explaining the fields, meanings, permitted values, and units in a dataset.

examples.en: The data dictionary explains why the example file contains two different fields for rainfall.
examples.zh: 「数据字典」解释了示例文件为什么有两个不同的降雨量字段。

examples.en: We used the data dictionary to check which unit the garden height column uses.
examples.zh: 我们用「数据字典」确认花园数据中高度列使用的单位。

words.enDefinition: Descriptive information about a dataset, including details such as its creator, subject, or coverage.

examples.en: The dataset metadata gives the publication date and the period covered by the rainfall readings.
examples.zh: 「数据集元数据」给出了发布日期和降雨量读数覆盖的时段。

examples.en: We updated the dataset metadata when the teaching team released a corrected copy of the file.
examples.zh: 教学团队发布更正后的文件副本时，我们更新了「数据集元数据」。

words.enDefinition: Material explaining how a dataset was collected, organized, and intended to be interpreted or used.

examples.en: The dataset documentation explains why the garden sensor collected fewer readings during the final week.
examples.zh: 「数据集文档」说明了花园传感器为何在最后一周采集到较少读数。

examples.en: Our class read the dataset documentation before selecting columns for the library attendance figure.
examples.zh: 我们班先读「数据集文档」，再为图书馆客流图挑选数据列。

words.enDefinition: A formal reference identifying the dataset used and giving the information needed to locate it.

examples.en: We added a dataset citation to the report so readers could find the original garden records.
examples.zh: 我们在报告里加了「数据集引用」，方便读者找到原始花园记录。

examples.en: The dataset citation specifies the version of the public table used for the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 「数据集引用」注明课堂练习用的是公开表格的哪个版本。

collocations: dataset citation with a persistent identifier

words.enDefinition: A stable reference assigned to a digital object so that it can remain identifiable over time.

examples.en: The dataset has a persistent identifier that remains the same when its download page moves.
examples.zh: 该数据集有一个「持久标识符」，即使下载页面迁移也保持不变。

examples.en: We copied the persistent identifier from the citation to locate the exact teaching example.
examples.zh: 我们从引文复制「持久标识符」，以定位指定的教学示例。

words.enDefinition: A specific published or saved state of a dataset distinguished from other states.

examples.en: The report states which dataset version contains the corrected library counts for the final week.
examples.zh: 报告写明哪个「数据集版本」包含更正后的最后一周图书馆客流量。

examples.en: Our sample chart changed because the class used a newer dataset version for the workshop.
examples.zh: 工作坊上，全班用了较新的「数据集版本」，示例图随之变化。

words.enDefinition: A fixed copy of data from a particular time whose contents are kept unchanged.

examples.en: The class kept an immutable data snapshot so subsequent edits would not affect the original analysis.
examples.zh: 全班保存了一份「不可变数据快照」，这样后续编辑就不会影响原始分析。

examples.en: We opened the immutable data snapshot to check the inputs used in the submitted report.
examples.zh: 我们打开「不可变数据快照」，核查提交报告时所用的输入数据。

collocations: immutable data snapshot from a given date

words.enDefinition: An initial value used to set up a pseudorandom generator so its sequence can be produced again under the same conditions.

examples.en: We recorded the random seed so the class could reproduce the same simulated rainfall values.
examples.zh: 我们记录了「随机种子」，让全班都能复现同一组模拟降雨量。

examples.en: The worksheet shows where the random seed is set before the example data are generated.
examples.zh: 练习纸标出生成示例数据前设置「随机种子」的位置。

words.enDefinition: A computed value used to check whether the contents of an input file match the recorded copy.

examples.en: The source file checksum matched the one recorded with the public rainfall data we downloaded.
examples.zh: 我们下载的公开降雨量数据的「源文件校验和」与记录的数值一致。

examples.en: We saved the source file checksum next to the input filename in the course archive.
examples.zh: 我们在课程档案中把「源文件校验和」保存在输入文件名旁边。

words.enDefinition: A file or record listing the inputs for a particular workflow, typically with identifying details.

examples.en: The input manifest lists two public tables and the version information for both source files.
examples.zh: 「输入清单」列出两张公开表及这两个源文件的版本信息。

examples.en: We compared the input manifest with the contents of the folder before starting the analysis.
examples.zh: 开始分析前，我们把「输入清单」与文件夹里的内容作了核对。

collocations: sources listed in the input manifest

words.enDefinition: Code saved in a file that carries out one or more steps of an analysis.

examples.en: The analysis script reads the public garden records and calculates the rainfall totals by week.
examples.zh: 「分析脚本」读取公开的花园记录，并计算每周降雨总量。

examples.en: We added a comment in the analysis script explaining the unit used for each measurement.
examples.zh: 我们在「分析脚本」里加了一条注释，说明各项测量所用的单位。

words.enDefinition: A file that supplies values used to configure a run of a program or analysis.

examples.en: The parameter file sets the date range for generating the classroom library attendance chart.
examples.zh: 「参数文件」设置生成课堂图书馆客流图的日期范围。

examples.en: We kept the analysis code unchanged and selected a different month in the parameter file.
examples.zh: 我们在「参数文件」中改选另一个月份，沿用同一份分析代码。

words.enDefinition: A configurable value that controls how an analysis is run or which inputs it uses.

examples.en: We recorded the date range as an analysis parameter so classmates could regenerate the figure.
examples.zh: 我们把日期范围记录为一项「分析参数」，方便同学重新生成图表。

examples.en: Changing one analysis parameter lets the workshop example calculate weekly totals for a different month.
examples.zh: 改动一个「分析参数」就能让工作坊示例计算另一个月份的每周总量。

words.enDefinition: The combination of software, versions, settings, and computing resources used to run an analysis.

examples.en: The report describes the computational environment so readers can see which software produced the figure.
examples.zh: 报告说明了「计算环境」，读者可以了解生成图表时用了哪些软件。

examples.en: We recreated the computational environment before comparing our output with the instructor's sample report.
examples.zh: 我们重建了「计算环境」，再将输出与老师的示例报告作比较。

words.enDefinition: A file or document listing the software and settings needed to recreate a computing environment.

examples.en: The environment specification lists the interpreter and the packages used to generate the example table.
examples.zh: 「环境配置说明」列出生成示例表时所用的解释器和软件包。

examples.en: Our group read the environment specification before trying to reproduce the two classroom figures.
examples.zh: 我们组先读了「环境配置说明」，再尝试复现两张课堂图表。

words.enDefinition: A file recording resolved dependency versions so later installations can reproduce the same selection.

examples.en: The dependency lockfile records the exact package versions used in the successful analysis run.
examples.zh: 「依赖锁定文件」记录成功运行分析时使用的软件包的确切版本。

examples.en: We checked the dependency lockfile after finding different library versions on the two classroom computers.
examples.zh: 我们发现两台教室电脑上的库版本不同，随后查看了「依赖锁定文件」。

words.enDefinition: To specify an exact dependency version instead of allowing a choice among versions.

examples.en: We decided to pin a dependency because its latest version drew tick labels differently.
examples.zh: 我们决定「固定依赖版本」，因为这个依赖的最新版绘制刻度标签的方式不同。

examples.en: The tutorial shows when to pin a dependency in a project with shared analysis scripts.
examples.zh: 教程展示了在共享分析脚本的项目中何时「固定依赖版本」。

collocations: pin a dependency to a version
pin a dependency in the environment file

words.enDefinition: An interactive document combining executable code, explanatory text, and the results it produces.

examples.en: Our computational notebook contains the code, comments, and chart for the rainfall exercise.
examples.zh: 我们的「计算笔记本」包含降雨量练习所需的代码、注释和图表。

examples.en: I opened the computational notebook to review the calculation just above the displayed table.
examples.zh: 我打开「计算笔记本」，查看结果表正上方的计算过程。

words.enDefinition: The sequence in which the code cells in a computational notebook are run.

examples.en: The notebook execution order matters because the last cell needs values created in earlier cells.
examples.zh: 「笔记本执行顺序」很重要，因为最后一个单元格要用到先前单元格生成的值。

examples.en: We checked notebook execution order after the same notebook produced different charts in class.
examples.zh: 同一个笔记本在课堂上生成不同图表后，我们核查了「笔记本执行顺序」。

collocations: notebook execution order from top to bottom

words.enDefinition: Values or settings from earlier actions that affect a computation without being declared in the current run.

examples.en: Hidden state from an earlier notebook cell changed the result in our classroom example.
examples.zh: 课堂示例中，先前笔记本单元格的「隐藏状态」改变了计算结果。

examples.en: We traced the hidden state to a table that was still loaded from a previous run.
examples.zh: 我们追溯到「隐藏状态」来自上一轮运行后仍然在内存里的表格。

words.enDefinition: A run that starts from a fresh state without relying on values or artefacts from earlier runs.

examples.en: A clean run reproduced the table using only the documented files and settings in our project.
examples.zh: 一次「从干净状态运行」仅用了项目文档列出的文件和设置，就复现了表格。

examples.en: We did a clean run to check that the notebook could recreate the original chart.
examples.zh: 我们让笔记本「从干净状态运行」，确认它能重新生成原图。

words.enDefinition: Execution that produces the same result when the relevant inputs and conditions are the same.

examples.en: The teaching script uses deterministic execution so the same input table always yields the same totals.
examples.zh: 教学脚本采用「确定性执行」，使相同的输入表始终得出同样的总量。

examples.en: Our report explains how deterministic execution lets reviewers compare the two runs figure by figure.
examples.zh: 报告说明「确定性执行」如何让审阅者逐图比较两次运行的结果。

words.enDefinition: A record of the events, messages, and timing from an individual program or workflow run.

examples.en: The run log shows when the rainfall calculation finished and when the chart was created.
examples.zh: 「运行日志」记载了降雨量计算完成和图表生成的时间。

examples.en: We saved the run log to explain why the table appeared before the chart in class.
examples.zh: 我们保存了「运行日志」，用它说明为什么课堂上先输出了表格。

words.enDefinition: A value that uniquely identifies one execution of a workflow within its recording system.

examples.en: The output folder includes a run identifier so we can match it to the correct log.
examples.zh: 输出文件夹含有「运行标识符」，让我们能把它与正确的日志对应起来。

examples.en: We recorded the run identifier beside the date and dataset version in the project notes.
examples.zh: 我们把「运行标识符」记在项目笔记的日期和数据集版本旁边。

words.enDefinition: A file or other saved output produced by running an analysis, such as a table or chart.

examples.en: Each analysis artefact is saved with a name that describes its content and reporting period.
examples.zh: 每份「分析产物」保存时的名称都会说明其内容和报告时段。

examples.en: The final chart is an analysis artefact generated directly by the same classroom script.
examples.zh: 最终图表是由同一个课堂脚本直接生成的「分析产物」。

words.enDefinition: A check that compares the results from repeating an analysis under the documented conditions.

examples.en: Our reproducibility check compared the totals and figures generated from the same public library data.
examples.zh: 我们的「可复现性检查」比较了用同一组公开图书馆数据生成的总量和图表。

examples.en: The team scheduled a reproducibility check before adding the final figures to the shared report.
examples.zh: 团队安排在把最终图表加进共享报告前做一次「可复现性检查」。

words.enDefinition: A collection of code, data or input references, and instructions for reproducing a reported result.

examples.en: The reproducibility package includes the scripts and a reference to the archived public data.
examples.zh: 「复现材料包」包含脚本和一条指向已归档公开数据的引用。

examples.en: We tested the reproducibility package on a different classroom computer before submitting the report.
examples.zh: 我们提交报告前，在教室的另一台电脑上测试了「复现材料包」。

words.enDefinition: The principles used to judge whether collecting, analysing, sharing, or using data is responsible.

examples.en: The class discussed data ethics before deciding which fields belonged in the public example table.
examples.zh: 全班讨论了「数据伦理」，再决定应在公开示例表中保留哪些字段。

examples.en: Our data ethics exercise asks whether a chart fairly represents the residents of smaller districts.
examples.zh: 我们的「数据伦理」练习要求判断图表是否公允地呈现人口较少地区的居民。

collocations: apply data ethics to a project

words.enDefinition: The roles, policies, and decision processes that guide how an organisation manages its data.

examples.en: The data governance policy identifies who approves changes to the fictional city's public dataset.
examples.zh: 「数据治理」政策说明由谁批准对虚构城市的公开数据集进行修改。

examples.en: We used a simple data governance model to assign responsibility for each classroom data file.
examples.zh: 我们用一个简单的「数据治理」模型来明确每个课堂数据文件由谁负责。

words.enDefinition: The ongoing responsibility for keeping data documented, usable, and properly managed.

examples.en: Her data stewardship duties include checking the file descriptions and maintaining the public dataset inventory.
examples.zh: 她的「数据管护」职责包括检查文件描述，以及维护公开数据集清单。

examples.en: The course uses data stewardship to discuss caring for archives after a project team disbands.
examples.zh: 课程借助「数据管护」这一概念，讨论项目组解散后如何管理档案。

words.enDefinition: A person or organisation responsible for the practical storage, protection, or maintenance of data.

examples.en: The data custodian keeps the archived teaching files available to approved course staff.
examples.zh: 「数据保管人」保存教学档案，供获准访问的课程工作人员使用。

examples.en: Our scenario names a data custodian who maintains the published files and their accompanying records.
examples.zh: 我们在情境设定中指定一位「数据保管人」，负责维护已发布的文件及随附记录。

words.enDefinition: Information about a person who is identified or could be identified.

examples.en: The fictional survey asks students to identify which fields would contain personal data in practice.
examples.zh: 虚构调查练习要求学生找出实际调查中哪些字段会含有「个人数据」。

examples.en: Our example release avoids personal data by showing only totals for the library branches.
examples.zh: 示例发布表只列各图书馆分馆的总量，避免包含「个人数据」。

words.enDefinition: Personal data whose nature or context calls for particular care because disclosure could cause substantial harm.

examples.en: The privacy exercise describes health information as an example of sensitive personal data requiring extra care.
examples.zh: 隐私练习把健康信息列为需要额外保护的「敏感个人数据」示例。

examples.en: Our classroom case asks why sensitive personal data should be kept out of the public attachment.
examples.zh: 我们的课堂案例要求解释为什么公开附件应避免包含「敏感个人数据」。

words.enDefinition: A value such as a name or unique assigned number that directly identifies a person.

examples.en: The worksheet classifies a full name as a direct identifier in its fictional registration table.
examples.zh: 练习纸把虚构登记表里的完整姓名归为「直接标识符」。

examples.en: We marked each direct identifier on the example form before considering what the published table needs.
examples.zh: 在考虑公开表格需要哪些字段之前，我们标出了示例表单上的所有「直接标识符」。

words.enDefinition: A feature that may help distinguish a person when combined with other information.

examples.en: The review considers whether a detailed location could serve as an indirect identifier in the example.
examples.zh: 审查会考虑详细地点在示例中是否可能充当「间接标识符」。

examples.en: The workshop asks why an indirect identifier may still deserve attention after names are removed.
examples.zh: 工作坊要求解释为什么去掉姓名后，「间接标识符」仍可能值得关注。

words.enDefinition: The treatment of data to remove or weaken links to the people described and reduce disclosure risk.

examples.en: The privacy worksheet presents de-identification as one way to reduce risk before releasing a table.
examples.zh: 隐私练习把「去标识化」列为降低表格发布风险的一种方式。

examples.en: We discussed de-identification while reading the privacy notes that accompanied an example public dataset.
examples.zh: 阅读示例公开数据集附带的隐私说明时，我们讨论了「去标识化」。

words.enDefinition: The replacement of identifiers with substitutes so linking records to a person requires separately held information.

examples.en: Our pseudonymisation example uses invented study codes and keeps the matching list in a separate worksheet.
examples.zh: 「假名化」示例用了虚构研究编号，并把对应清单保存在另一张工作表里。

examples.en: The report explains why pseudonymisation alone does not make the classroom records suitable for public release.
examples.zh: 报告解释了为何仅做「假名化」，还不足以让课堂记录适合公开。

words.enDefinition: Artificially generated data used in place of actual observations to serve a particular purpose.

examples.en: The course uses synthetic data to teach plotting without including any actual students' attendance records.
examples.zh: 课程使用「合成数据」教授绘图，示例中没有任何学生的真实出勤记录。

examples.en: We labelled the figures as synthetic data so readers would recognise the numbers as simulated.
examples.zh: 我们标注图中数值来自「合成数据」，让读者知道这些数据是模拟的。

words.enDefinition: Data combined into summaries for groups rather than shown as individual records.

examples.en: The published table contains aggregate data for each library branch across the whole teaching term.
examples.zh: 公布的表格包含教学学期内各图书馆分馆的「汇总数据」。

examples.en: We plotted aggregate data so each bar represents an entire reading group's total number of visits.
examples.zh: 我们绘制了「汇总数据」，每个条形表示一个阅读小组的到访总量。

words.enDefinition: Record-level data about individual units such as people, households, or establishments.

examples.en: The class compared microdata with a summary table to see what each row represents.
examples.zh: 全班比较了「微观数据」和汇总表，看看每行各自代表什么。

examples.en: The example microdata contain one fictional record for each household in the training exercise.
examples.zh: 示例「微观数据」为练习中的每户家庭提供一条虚构记录。

words.enDefinition: The possibility that sharing data would reveal protected information about the units they describe.

examples.en: The review considers disclosure risk before the team publishes the example district attendance table.
examples.zh: 团队发布示例各区客流表之前，审查会考虑「披露风险」。

examples.en: We wrote a short note explaining how the proposed chart changes could reduce disclosure risk.
examples.zh: 我们写了一段简短说明，解释拟议的图表改动如何降低「披露风险」。

words.enDefinition: Measures that reduce the chance that published statistics reveal confidential information about individual units.

examples.en: Statistical disclosure control helps protect confidentiality in the example table of attendance by neighbourhood.
examples.zh: 「统计披露控制」有助于保护示例社区客流表中的信息机密性。

examples.en: The course notes describe statistical disclosure control before introducing the exercise on public summary tables.
examples.zh: 课程讲义先说明「统计披露控制」，再介绍公开汇总表的练习。

collocations: statistical disclosure control for tabular data

words.enDefinition: Withholding selected values from a released table to protect confidential information.

examples.en: The published example uses cell suppression to protect information about a very small group.
examples.zh: 发布示例用「单元格抑制」保护一个人数很少的群体的信息。

examples.en: The note beneath the table tells readers where cell suppression affected the published values.
examples.zh: 表下说明告知读者哪些公布数值受到了「单元格抑制」的影响。

collocations: use cell suppression in a table

words.enDefinition: A low count in a statistical table cell that may require special review before release.

examples.en: The reviewer flagged a small cell count before the sample district table was made public.
examples.zh: 示例区域表公开前，审查员标记了一个「单元格低计数」。

examples.en: We discussed when a small cell count in a classroom table might warrant an extra check.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了课堂表格出现「单元格低计数」时，哪些情况可能需要额外核查。

words.enDefinition: A character used in a table to indicate that a value has been withheld.

examples.en: The footnote explains that the suppression symbol marks a withheld value in the example table.
examples.zh: 表下注解释「抑制标记」表示示例表中有一个数值未公开。

examples.en: Our class distinguished the suppression symbol from the zero shown for another category.
examples.zh: 全班区分了「抑制标记」和另一个类别显示的零。

words.enDefinition: An examination of information before release to check for confidentiality or privacy concerns.

examples.en: The example table goes through disclosure review before it is added to the public report.
examples.zh: 示例表在写入公开报告之前要经过「披露审查」。

examples.en: Our project notes say who completed the disclosure review and which version was examined.
examples.zh: 项目笔记写明谁完成了「披露审查」，以及审查的是哪个版本。

words.enDefinition: The practice of collecting and keeping only the data needed for a stated purpose.

examples.en: Data minimisation led the group to request attendance totals without collecting individual names for the exercise.
examples.zh: 按照「数据最小化」原则，小组只索取练习所需的出席总量，没有收集姓名。

examples.en: The tutor used data minimisation to explain why the example form asks for fewer details.
examples.zh: 老师用「数据最小化」解释了为什么示例表单要求填写的细节较少。

words.enDefinition: The principle of using data only for specified purposes or compatible purposes that have been justified.

examples.en: The purpose limitation in our case study confines the data use to the agreed teaching exercise.
examples.zh: 案例里的「目的限制」规定，数据只用于约定的教学练习。

examples.en: The class discussed purpose limitation when a group suggested using survey responses for another project.
examples.zh: 有小组建议把问卷回答用于另一项项目时，全班讨论了「目的限制」。

words.enDefinition: A record stating how long different kinds of data are kept and when they are reviewed or removed.

examples.en: The data retention schedule tells the fictional team when it should review its teaching files.
examples.zh: 「数据留存计划表」告诉虚构团队何时复查教学文件。

examples.en: Our case study compares the entries for raw records and published totals in the data retention schedule.
examples.zh: 案例比较了「数据留存计划表」中原始记录与公开总量各自对应的条目。

words.enDefinition: Data released for use by the general public, subject to any applicable terms of use.

examples.en: The class selected public-use data for the exercise so everyone could access the same records.
examples.zh: 全班为练习选了「公开使用数据」，方便每个人都能取得相同记录。

examples.en: The documentation for the public-use data explains how the example dataset differs from the original records.
examples.zh: 「公开使用数据」的文档解释示例数据集与原始记录之间的区别。

words.enDefinition: Data available only to people who meet specified conditions or have obtained specific approval.

examples.en: The practice scenario reserves restricted-use data for approved analysts under a written agreement.
examples.zh: 练习情境规定，只有受书面协议约束的获准分析人员才能使用「限用数据」。

examples.en: We compared the documentation for restricted-use data with the notes accompanying the public file.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「限用数据」的文档和公开文件随附的说明。

collocations: apply for access to restricted-use data

words.enDefinition: An agreement setting conditions on who can use data and for what purposes.

examples.en: The data use agreement limits the example records to the agreed classroom analysis.
examples.zh: 「数据使用协议」把示例记录的用途限定为已约定的课堂分析。

examples.en: The team reviewed the data use agreement before writing its plans for the fictional dataset.
examples.zh: 团队在写出虚构数据集的使用计划前，先查阅了「数据使用协议」。

collocations: terms of a data use agreement

words.enDefinition: An agreement setting the terms and responsibilities for sharing data between parties.

examples.en: The data sharing agreement describes what each fictional institution may send to the other.
examples.zh: 「数据共享协议」说明两家虚构机构各自可以向对方发送哪些内容。

examples.en: We read the data sharing agreement to see which team maintains the approved public summary.
examples.zh: 我们查阅「数据共享协议」，确认哪一组负责维护已获批准的公开摘要。

collocations: enter into a data sharing agreement
responsibilities under a data sharing agreement

words.enDefinition: Formal permission for a person or group to use specified data under stated conditions.

examples.en: The project lead recorded data access approval before the team used the restricted teaching files.
examples.zh: 团队使用有限制的教学文件前，项目负责人记录了「数据访问批准」。

examples.en: Our example form describes which dataset and time period the data access approval covers.
examples.zh: 示例表单说明「数据访问批准」适用哪个数据集和哪个时段。

words.enDefinition: the terms under which a particular dataset may be accessed, copied, modified or distributed

examples.en: We checked the dataset licence before including a copy of the public table in our handout.
examples.zh: 我们把公开表格副本放进讲义之前，先查阅了「数据集许可」。

examples.en: The dataset licence requires credit when students reuse the example values in a published chart.
examples.zh: 「数据集许可」要求学生在已发布图表中使用示例数值时注明来源。

words.enDefinition: Whether the conditions of different licences can be met together for a proposed use.

examples.en: The class examined licence compatibility before combining two public datasets for the report.
examples.zh: 全班在合并报告所需的两个公开数据集之前，检查了「许可兼容性」。

examples.en: The worksheet asks which terms determine licence compatibility when a combined table is shared.
examples.zh: 练习题问共享合并表格时，哪些条款决定「许可兼容性」。

words.enDefinition: A condition that limits how people can use data after receiving or accessing it.

examples.en: One reuse restriction limits the teaching data to the exercises described in the course handout.
examples.zh: 一项「再利用限制」规定，教学数据只用于课程讲义所述的练习。

examples.en: We recorded the reuse restriction next to the source citation so it would be easy to find.
examples.zh: 我们把「再利用限制」记在资料引用旁边，以便查找。

words.enDefinition: A condition requiring users of a resource to credit its creator or source.

examples.en: The attribution requirement says to name the organisation that published the sample rainfall data.
examples.zh: 「署名要求」规定，应注明发布示例降雨数据的机构名称。

examples.en: The class fulfilled the attribution requirement by adding the source and creator below the chart.
examples.zh: 全班在图下补充了来源和创作者，满足了「署名要求」。

words.enDefinition: A review of how planned data handling or reporting could affect people's privacy.

examples.en: Our privacy risk assessment considers who can see the files at each stage of the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们的「隐私风险评估」会考虑在练习各阶段有哪些人能看到这些文件。

examples.en: The project team documented its privacy risk assessment before deciding how to publish the summaries.
examples.zh: 项目团队决定如何公布汇总信息前，记录了自己的「隐私风险评估」。

collocations: scope of a privacy risk assessment

words.enDefinition: The practice of considering and building in privacy protections from the start of a project or system.

examples.en: The privacy by design exercise asks students to consider confidentiality before building the example dashboard.
examples.zh: 「隐私保护融入设计」练习要求学生先考虑保密问题，再搭建示例仪表板。

examples.en: Our team discussed privacy by design while deciding what the classroom tool needed to collect.
examples.zh: 团队在决定课堂工具需要采集哪些信息时，讨论了「隐私保护融入设计」。

words.enDefinition: A structured review in which a team evaluates the ethical aspects of its own data project.

examples.en: The data ethics self-assessment asks the class to describe who might benefit from the report.
examples.zh: 「数据伦理自评」要求全班说清哪些人可能从这份报告中受益。

examples.en: We completed the data ethics self-assessment before deciding whether our example chart needed more context.
examples.zh: 我们先完成「数据伦理自评」，再决定是否为示例图表补充背景。
